ImageDescription.value: Large gourd calabash holds a quantity of dried purple hibiscus leaves for the popular beverage, 'bissap' (also spelled as bisap). Leaves are boiled, then strained out, leaving the distinctive dark purple tisane.  Very tart, so sugar and flavorings such as vanilla are added to taste for the basic recipe, additional flavors vary with household recipes.

Artist.value: Jamo Photography

ImageDescription.value: Fresh, fermented and dried market ingredients for this Senegalese paella-like rice pilaf garnished with whole fish and a distinctive paste blend made with nététou (fermented African locust bean/Parkia biglobosa);steamed fresh green Hibiscus sabdariffa leaves; and fried red capsicum. Recipe includes flavorings of one sachet of mixed dried 'fruit de mer', made up of five unique ingredients: chopped 'yet' (cured Cymbium marmoratum), Pañ – dried small clam (of the type senilia senilis); also 'touffa', a whelk; and 'yokhos' - dried oysters; plus dried shrimp. Fish is typically Dorade (French) (related to p. aurata), a bundle of fresh hibiscus (sabdariffa) leaves, plus red palm oil (Elaeis guineensis). Spellings of the Wolof names vary. (Rice, salt to taste and cooking oil not shown).

Artist.value: T.K. Naliaka

39251244.title: File:Thiéboudiène Boukhonk with tamarind - ingredients, dry detail.jpg

ImageDescription.value: Detail of the flavorings that distinguish this Senegalese rice pilaf with fish dish,also seen written as ceebu jen, (Wolof ceebu for rice, jen for fish). Here black peppers, red capsicum, fermented tamarind seed pods (Tamarindus indica), dry hibiscus leaves, displayed as sold pre-measured in small plastic sachets in the market (shown compared to a teaspoon), and all together shown are the actual quantities used for one complete family/communal size meal. The name Thiéboudiène Boukhonk is from Wolof language, spellings vary: thiéboudiène uses the French alphabet spelling, ceebu jen is the same word using the official Senegalese alphabet spelling). Also names of this popular West African dish vary between languages and countries.

Artist.value: T.K. Naliaka

ImageDescription.value: It’s a popular West African beverage made from dried hibiscus petals (usually Hibiscus sabdariffa), often flavored with ginger, pineapple, cloves, or other spices knows as Agua de Jamaica in (Mexico)

Zobo drink is a neighborhood refreshment drink in Nigeria. It is produced using dried hibiscus leaf and different fixings. The beverage is regularly sold in cafés and on side of the road. Zobo drinks are served at parties events and it tends to be taken as family refreshment drink. three sorts of Hibiscus sabdariffa utilized in zobo drink readiness are the dim red, radiant red, and wine-shaded assortments, while the leaves are utilized in soup arrangements, and the oil from the seeds is viewed as a wellspring of healthful minerals.
